messages.author: 75d9bfea53492f3f
messages.subject: not recognizing WHERE on a column of class logical
parts:
Hello, thank you so much for any help!

This works:

shallow_Dem_jur<-sqldf('
SELECT country,COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no) FROM sponge WHERE period="Jurassic" AND class_name="Demospongea"
GROUP BY country
')

shallow_Dem_jur
country COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no)
1 Algeria 5
2 Argentina 1
3 Austria 17
4 Canada 7
5 China 29 #... etc

But this does not work:

shallow_Dem_jur<-sqldf('
SELECT country,COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no) FROM sponge_sql WHERE period="Jurassic" AND class_name="Demospongea" AND above_fair_wb="TRUE"
GROUP BY country
')

Nor does this:

shallow_Dem_jur<-sqldf('
SELECT country,COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no) FROM sponge_sql WHERE above_fair_wb="TRUE"
GROUP BY country
')

All I get is:

shallow_Dem_jur
[1] country COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no)
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

The only difference I can tell is that the columns period and class_name are of class character, but the column above_fair_wb is of class logical.

I tried to fix this with

class(sponge_sql[,77])<-as.character(sponge_sql[,77])

But the column is STILL logical.

How can I either fix the columns to be character class, or how do I properly frame a WHERE clause for logical vectors?

Thanks! This is day 3 of sqldf and it's working wonders but I'm still getting stuck hourly.

- Kathleen, a paleontologist

SQLite does not have a logical / boolean datatype.  TRUE will become 1 and FALSE will become 0.  For example,

> DF <- data.frame(a = 1:3, b = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
> sqldf("select * from DF where b = 0")
  a     b
1 3 FALSE
> sqldf("select * from DF where b = 1")
  a    b
1 1 TRUE
2 2 TRUE

The H2 database, which is also supported by sqldf, does have a boolean data type so with it we can do this:

> library(RH2)
Loading required package: RJDBC
Loading required package: rJava
> sqldf("select * from DF where b = 'TRUE'")
  a    b
1 1 TRUE
2 2 TRUE
> sqldf("select * from DF where b = 'FALSE'")
  a     b
1 3 FALSE
